cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. We're still listening to the words of the wise, and the teacher talks to his listener like a dad. He calls him "My son," and he starts with what makes HIS heart happy.

cards.question: The teacher says his own heart will rejoice. What would do it?
The teacher says his inmost being will rejoice when his son's lips speak what is right.

cards.text: Then a warning: "Do not let your heart envy sinners." I know, friend. Some days the guy parked in the fire lane gets the best spot EVERY. SINGLE. TIME.

cards.question: Instead of envying sinners, what does the teacher tell his son to always continue in?

cards.text: And he says why it's worth sticking with: "For surely there is a future." Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer. Trust me, that's a line you want somebody to say to you.

cards.question: The teacher tells his son that his hope will be cut off.

cards.text: "Listen, my son, and be wise, and guide your heart on the right course." Then he points out a crowd his son should stay away from.

cards.question: Which crowd does the teacher tell his son not to join?
The teacher says the drunkard and the glutton will come to ___.

cards.text: And he adds, "drowsiness will clothe them in rags." Believe me. Years lying around in a junk drawer, and you know what my whole outfit was? DUST. Head to toe. Designer dust.
Now the teacher brings it home: "Listen to your father who gave you life." Then he has a word about the son's mother too.

cards.question: What does the teacher tell the son about his mother?

answers.text: Do not despise her when she is old
Do not leave her when you marry
Do not argue with her at the gate

cards.text: Then he sounds like a financial advisor. "Invest in truth," he says, "in wisdom and instruction and understanding." FINALLY. An investment I don't have to check every five minutes on my phone.

cards.question: The teacher says to invest in truth and never ___ it.

cards.text: Then the teacher comes back around to where he started: what a son like that means to his father.

cards.question: The teacher says the father of a righteous man will worry over him.

cards.text: He closes with a blessing: "May your father and mother be glad, and may she who gave you birth rejoice!" Me? Nobody gave me birth, friend. A quarter got me home. And Mother Miller STILL smiled.
"My son, give me your heart," the teacher says, "and let your eyes delight in my ways." Then he warns his son about the prostitute and the adulteress.

cards.question: What pictures does the teacher use for the prostitute and the adulteress?

answers.text: A deep pit and a narrow well
A strong tower and a high wall
A green field and a quiet stream

cards.text: Then he adds one more picture: "Like a robber she lies in wait."

cards.question: Like a robber she lies in wait and multiplies the ___ among men.

cards.text: Then the teacher fires off questions like a game show host: "Who has woe? Who has sorrow? Who has contentions? Who has complaints? Who has needless wounds? Who has bloodshot eyes?" Six questions. No commercial break. I'm out of breath just READING it.

cards.question: So who has all that woe, sorrow and those bloodshot eyes?

cards.text: Then he describes wine looking its very best. Red, sparkling in the cup, going down smoothly.

cards.question: The teacher tells his son to gaze at the wine while it sparkles in the cup.
Wine goes down smoothly. But what does the teacher say it does in the end?

cards.text: "In the end it bites like a snake and stings like a viper." It's like a cookie that's golden on top, then you flip it over and the bottom is BLACK. Smooth start. Rough ending.

cards.question: The teacher says the drinker's eyes will see ___ things and his mind will utter perversities.
The teacher says the drinker will be like someone sleeping safe in his own bed.

cards.text: Nope. He'll be like one sleeping on the high seas, or lying on the top of a mast. The TOP of the MAST. Friend, I wobble on my gold base, and that thing is FLAT.
Then the teacher lets the drinker talk: "They struck me, but I feel no pain! They beat me, but I did not know it!"

cards.question: The drinker got beaten and didn't even know it. What does he want to do once he wakes up?

answers.text: Find the men who hit him

cards.text: "When can I wake up to search for another drink?" Beat up, and his first plan is round two. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. The wise aren't done talking yet.

findings.problem: The question types follow a pattern in both stops, and the two stops share it. Multiple choice fills every other choice slot at the start of each stop. Stop 1 runs MC, TF, MC, TF, MC, FB, MC, FB, TF. Stop 2 runs MC, FB, MC, TF, MC, FB, TF, MC.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
